metadata.header: Porto Taxi Stand and Driver Demand across Operating Conditions
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed set of 1,200 Porto taxi trips from 20 drivers across ordinary and genuine pre-holiday operating-shift dates. Twelve named taxi stands, three service channels, three time periods, matched driver pairs, and dense OSM-road-aligned GPS paths support four complementary demand analyses.

insights: Taxi demand is uneven across stands, with a small group consistently receiving substantially more trips than most other stands.
The busiest taxi stands change across the day, with some peaking in daytime and others becoming relatively more active during evening periods.
Some drivers are more stand-oriented during daytime, while others become increasingly street-hail-oriented toward evening and night.
Pre-holiday periods change the taxi call-type mix more strongly for some drivers than for drivers with otherwise similar weekday patterns.
summary: Stand demand is concentrated but its leaders change over the day. Driver groups differ in daytime stand reliance and evening street-hail growth, and matched drivers with similar ordinary-day channel mixes can respond very differently before holidays.
